claims.title: Bantu farmers settle the plateau
claims.summary: Bantu-speaking migrants bringing iron-working, cattle, and agriculture spread across the region over the first millennium CE, gradually settling land held by Khoisan and Batwa hunter-gatherers.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-300-bantu-farmers-settle-the-plateau, claim TL:ZMB:event:300:bantu-farmers-settle-the-plateau, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Tonga of the Zambezi
claims.summary: On the southern plateau the Tonga and related Ila peoples established dispersed farming communities along the middle Zambezi, organised by lineage rather than centralised kingship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1000-the-tonga-of-the-zambezi, claim TL:ZMB:event:1000:the-tonga-of-the-zambezi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Trade at Ingombe Ilede
claims.summary: The Iron Age settlement of Ingombe Ilede near the Zambezi yielded copper crosses, gold, and imported beads and cloth, showing the region's links to the Indian Ocean trade in gold and ivory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1450-trade-at-ingombe-ilede, claim TL:ZMB:event:1450:trade-at-ingombe-ilede, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Lozi kingdom
claims.summary: On the upper Zambezi floodplain the Luyana (Aluyi) people, of Lunda origin, built the Lozi (Barotse) kingdom ruled by a king titled the Litunga, with capitals that shifted with the annual flood.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1600-rise-of-the-lozi-kingdom, claim TL:ZMB:event:1600:rise-of-the-lozi-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Kazembe kingdom
claims.summary: An offshoot of the Lunda crossed the Luapula River, subdued the Shila, and established the kingdom of the Mwata Kazembe, which grew wealthy on Lake Mweru fisheries and trade in copper, salt, and ivory.

sources.label: Zambia: External contacts and the slave and ivory trade

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1700-founding-of-the-kazembe-kingdom, claim TL:ZMB:event:1700:founding-of-the-kazembe-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lacerda reaches Kazembe
claims.summary: A Portuguese expedition under Francisco de Lacerda reached the court of the Mwata Kazembe seeking to open trade links across the continent, an early European contact with the Luapula kingdom.

sources.label: Zambia: External contacts and the slave and ivory trade

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1798-lacerda-reaches-kazembe, claim TL:ZMB:event:1798:lacerda-reaches-kazembe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gamitto's mission to Kazembe
claims.summary: A second Portuguese expedition, led by António Gamitto, visited the Mwata Kazembe, leaving a detailed account of a Lunda state deeply engaged in the regional trade in ivory, copper, and captives.

sources.label: Zambia: External contacts and the slave and ivory trade

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1831-gamitto-s-mission-to-kazembe, claim TL:ZMB:event:1831:gamitto-s-mission-to-kazembe, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kololo conquest of the Lozi
claims.summary: The Kololo, a Sotho people fleeing the wars of the Mfecane under Sebitwane, crossed the Zambezi and conquered the Lozi kingdom, imposing their rule and language on the floodplain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1840-kololo-conquest-of-the-lozi, claim TL:ZMB:event:1840:kololo-conquest-of-the-lozi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ngoni incursions from the south
claims.summary: Ngoni warbands driven north by the upheavals of the Mfecane crossed the Zambezi under leaders such as Zwangendaba, raiding and absorbing peoples and settling in the east of the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1835-ngoni-incursions-from-the-south, claim TL:ZMB:event:1835:ngoni-incursions-from-the-south, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Livingstone reaches Victoria Falls
claims.summary: Guided by local people, David Livingstone became the first European recorded to see the falls the inhabitants called Mosi-oa-Tunya, renaming them Victoria Falls and drawing European attention to the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1855-livingstone-reaches-victoria-falls, claim TL:ZMB:event:1855:livingstone-reaches-victoria-falls, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Swahili-Arab and Chikunda slave trade
claims.summary: Swahili-Arab traders from the coast and Chikunda raiders from the Zambezi, with Bisa and Yao intermediaries, exchanged guns and cloth for ivory and captives, bringing violence and depopulation to the plateau.

sources.label: Zambia: External contacts and the slave and ivory trade

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1860-swahili-arab-and-chikunda-slave-trade, claim TL:ZMB:event:1860:swahili-arab-and-chikunda-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lozi restoration under Sipopa
claims.summary: A Lozi rebellion overthrew Kololo rule and restored the kingdom under Sipopa, reviving the indigenous monarchy of the upper Zambezi floodplain.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1864-lozi-restoration-under-sipopa, claim TL:ZMB:event:1864:lozi-restoration-under-sipopa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Lochner Concession
claims.summary: The Lozi king Lewanika granted mineral rights to Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company in exchange for promises of protection, opening the territory to company rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1890-the-lochner-concession, claim TL:ZMB:event:1890:the-lochner-concession, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Creation of Northern Rhodesia
claims.summary: The British South Africa Company amalgamated North-Western and North-Eastern Rhodesia into a single territory named Northern Rhodesia, administered under royal charter.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1911-creation-of-northern-rhodesia, claim TL:ZMB:event:1911:creation-of-northern-rhodesia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Northern Rhodesia becomes a Crown protectorate
claims.summary: Administration passed from the British South Africa Company to the Colonial Office, making Northern Rhodesia a British protectorate; the capital later moved to Lusaka in 1935.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1924-northern-rhodesia-becomes-a-crown-protectorate, claim TL:ZMB:event:1924:northern-rhodesia-becomes-a-crown-protectorate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Copperbelt copper proven
claims.summary: Rich copper sulphide ores were proven beneath the Copperbelt, and large-scale mining from the 1930s built the industrial economy that came to dominate the territory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1928-copperbelt-copper-proven, claim TL:ZMB:event:1928:copperbelt-copper-proven, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Copperbelt mineworkers' strike
claims.summary: African mineworkers struck over taxes and conditions; six men were shot dead during the disturbances, an early sign of the labour grievances that would fuel nationalist politics. Further strikes followed in 1940.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1935-copperbelt-mineworkers-strike, claim TL:ZMB:event:1935:copperbelt-mineworkers-strike, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland
claims.summary: Britain joined Northern Rhodesia, Southern Rhodesia, and Nyasaland into a federation dominated by white settlers, provoking widespread African opposition and galvanising nationalist politics.

sources.label: Formation of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1953-federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland, claim TL:ZMB:event:1953:federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kaunda founds ZANC
claims.summary: Breaking with Harry Nkumbula's ANC, Kenneth Kaunda founded the radical Zambia African National Congress; it was banned in 1959 and Kaunda imprisoned, but the movement continued as UNIP.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1958-kaunda-founds-zanc, claim TL:ZMB:event:1958:kaunda-founds-zanc, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Cha-cha-cha campaign
claims.summary: Under Kaunda, UNIP launched a campaign of mass civil disobedience known as the Cha-cha-cha against colonial rule and the Federation, intensifying pressure for African self-government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1961-the-cha-cha-cha-campaign, claim TL:ZMB:event:1961:the-cha-cha-cha-campaign, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Federation dissolved
claims.summary: Sustained African opposition and shifting British policy brought the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland to an end, opening the way to independence for its territories.

sources.label: Formation of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1963-federation-dissolved, claim TL:ZMB:event:1963:federation-dissolved, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of Zambia
claims.summary: Northern Rhodesia became the independent Republic of Zambia, named after the Zambezi, with Kenneth Kaunda as its first president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1964-independence-of-zambia, claim TL:ZMB:event:1964:independence-of-zambia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: One-party state and Humanism
claims.summary: Kaunda made Zambia a one-party state under UNIP, formalised in the 1973 constitution, governing under his philosophy of Humanism, a blend of African communal values and socialism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1972-one-party-state-and-humanism, claim TL:ZMB:event:1972:one-party-state-and-humanism, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Copper collapse and economic decline
claims.summary: Copper, which provided the bulk of export earnings, fell sharply on the world market from the mid-1970s, triggering a long economic decline, rising debt, and austerity.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1975-copper-collapse-and-economic-decline, claim TL:ZMB:event:1975:copper-collapse-and-economic-decline, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Frontline state for liberation
claims.summary: Zambia hosted and supported southern African liberation movements, including the ANC, ZANU, ZAPU, and SWAPO, becoming a frontline state that bore retaliatory raids and economic costs.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1970-frontline-state-for-liberation, claim TL:ZMB:event:1970:frontline-state-for-liberation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to multiparty democracy
claims.summary: After food riots and mounting pressure, Kaunda lifted the ban on opposition parties; Frederick Chiluba and the Movement for Multiparty Democracy won the elections, and Kaunda handed over power peacefully.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-1991-return-to-multiparty-democracy, claim TL:ZMB:event:1991:return-to-multiparty-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sovereign debt default
claims.summary: Burdened by debt and falling revenues, Zambia became the first African country of the COVID-19 era to default on its Eurobonds after missing a coupon payment.

sources.label: The Road to Zambia's 2020 Sovereign Debt Default

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-2020-sovereign-debt-default, claim TL:ZMB:event:2020:sovereign-debt-default, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hichilema elected president
claims.summary: Opposition leader Hakainde Hichilema won the presidency in a decisive, peaceful election, taking office with a mandate to restructure the national debt and revive the copper-dependent economy.

sources.label: The Road to Zambia's 2020 Sovereign Debt Default

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Zambia: From Iron Age farmers and the kingdoms of the Zambezi and Luapula to the Copperbelt, Northern Rhodesia, and a landlocked African republic.", terralore.co/country/ZMB/chronicle#ev-2021-hichilema-elected-president, claim TL:ZMB:event:2021:hichilema-elected-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
